request.spec:
A button on each person's row downloads their row as a CSV file: a header line cell,value then one
line per cell for person-name, person-grade, person-claimed, person-due-total, person-statement-count,
person-overdue-total, person-hold, person-retired, person-aliases and person-score, in that order,
each with the value as the row shows it.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A button on each person's row downloads their row as a CSV file: a header line cell,value then one
line per cell for person-name, person-grade, person-claimed, person-due-total, person-statement-count,
person-overdue-total, person-hold, person-retired, person-aliases and person-score, in that order,
each with the value as the row shows it.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Each person's row now has an **Export** button that downloads the row as a CSV, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

The file starts with the header `cell,value`, then has one line for each of the ten cells in the order you listed, from `person-name` to `person-score`. A value containing a comma is quoted, so "Lee, Jo (B)" comes out as `"Lee, Jo (B)"`.

How it works (all in `src/main/frontend/src/app/features/people/people.ts`):
- **Values:** the export reads each value from the text the row actually displays, so it always matches the screen, including `person-claimed`, which a sub-component draws. This happens entirely in the browser, with no server or stored-data changes.
- **Hidden columns:** if a user has hidden one of these columns, that cell's value is exported blank. None of the tests hide columns, so this case isn't tested.
- **Reuse:** it uses the CSV quoting and download code the file already had for the other exports. The file is named `person-<id>-<sheet>.csv`.

I also moved an existing comment about CSV quoting that had ended up above the wrong function.
